quote: All things are difficult, before they are easy.
meaning: Everything is hard the first time. It gets easy later.

who: Russian proverb · V. I. Dal's collection, 1862
quote: The first pancake comes out a lump.
meaning: Your first try is usually messy. That is normal, so keep going.

who: Seneca · Letters to Lucilius 104, tr. Richard M. Gummere, 1925
quote: To what man did they not seem easier in the doing? Our lack of confidence is not the result of difficulty; the difficulty comes from our lack of confidence.
meaning: Things look hard because we are afraid to start. Once we start, they feel easier.

who: B. K. S. Iyengar · Light on Yoga, 1966
quote: Everything will seem at first to be completely unfamiliar... This is due to fear of a fall... To topple over while learning the head stand is not as terrible as we imagine... Then one will just roll over and smile.
meaning: Going upside down feels strange and scary at first. A fall is not as bad as you fear.

quote: When I first got into the water to swim... I didn't want to put my face under... Yes, me, Michael Phelps, afraid to put my face into the water. But naturally, you overcome those fears...
meaning: Even Michael Phelps was scared to put his face in the water at first. He got over it.

who: Russian proverb · V. I. Dal's collection, 1862
quote: The eyes frighten you, but the hands get it done.
meaning: Start, and your hands get it done.

who: Rikyu's hundred tea poems · tr. from Japanese
quote: Cast off shame, ask others, and learn: this is the very foundation of skill.
meaning: Feeling shy at the start is normal. Ask anyway. That is where every skill begins.

who: Sama, a Buddhist nun · Therigatha 2.10, tr. Bhikkhu Sujato & Jessica Walton, 2019
quote: Four or five times / I left my dwelling. / I had failed to find peace of heart, / or any control over my mind.
meaning: Even a nun who gave her life to practice found the start hard. You are not alone.

who: Su Shi · on Wen Yuke's bamboo painting, 1079, tr. from Chinese
quote: Yuke taught me this. I could not do it, though my mind understood why. ... Inside and outside are not one; mind and hand do not answer each other. That is the fault of not having practised.
meaning: Knowing it in your head is not enough. Your hands and body learn only by practice.

who: Goethe · Wilhelm Meister's Apprenticeship, tr. Thomas Carlyle, 1824
quote: The height charms us, the steps to it do not: with the summit in our eye, we love to walk along the plain.
meaning: We love the top, but not the steps to get there. The steps are the practice.
